title: Kia India Posts Record July Sales at 28,200 Units, Up 27%
excerpt: The Korean automaker's best-ever July performance brings year-to-date wholesale dispatches to nearly 1.92 lakh units, driven by Seltos, Sonet and new EV launches.
body:
• Kia India dispatched 28,200 units in July 2026, a 27.4% year-on-year increase over 22,135 units in July 2025 — the company's highest-ever July wholesale figure.
  • Year-to-date sales for January–July 2026 reached 1,91,949 units, up 16.85% over the same period last year, keeping Kia on track for its India sales target of 302,000 units.
  • The Seltos and Sonet SUVs remain core volume drivers, while the newly launched Syros EV and Carens Clavis EV are expanding Kia's electric vehicle footprint in the mass market.

Kia India reported wholesale dispatches of 28,200 units in July 2026, marking a 27.4% year-on-year jump from 22,135 units sold in July 2025. The figure represents the company's strongest-ever July performance since it began operations in India in 2019, according to data published by the automaker.

On a month-on-month basis, volumes climbed 14.86% from 24,552 units dispatched in June 2026. The July result pushed Kia's cumulative January–July 2026 sales to 1,91,949 units — a 16.85% increase over 1,64,274 units in the corresponding period last year.

SUV Lineup Anchors Growth

The Seltos mid-size SUV and Sonet compact SUV continued to account for the bulk of Kia's monthly volumes. In recent months, Seltos alone has contributed over 40% of Kia India's sales, with both models consistently crossing the 10,000-unit monthly mark. The Seltos carries a 5-star Bharat NCAP safety rating — the highest score among ICE vehicles tested to date — and has drawn a sizeable share of existing Kia owners upgrading to the refreshed model.

The Carens Clavis and its electric variant, the Carens Clavis EV, continued to deliver steady volumes in the MPV segment. Kia said its Battery-as-a-Service (BaaS) programme, which lowers upfront acquisition costs for electric vehicles, has helped broaden the EV's buyer base.

Syros EV Adds Momentum

Kia highlighted encouraging early bookings for the Syros EV, the company's second Made-in-India mass-market electric vehicle. Positioned in the compact electric SUV segment, the Syros EV offers an ARAI-certified range exceeding 500 km, DC fast charging and Level 2 advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS). The launch adds another entry point for EV buyers into Kia's portfolio alongside the Carens Clavis EV.

"Strong demand across our SUV and MPV lineup helped deliver the record July performance. The positive market response to the Syros EV is helping strengthen our presence in the growing mass-market EV space."

— Kia India

Where Kia Stands in the Market

Kia India holds the sixth position among the country's top passenger vehicle manufacturers, behind Maruti Suzuki, Tata Motors, Mahindra & Mahindra, Hyundai Motor India and Toyota Kirloskar Motor. In Q2 2026 (April–June), the six largest OEMs together sold 11.88 lakh passenger vehicles, with Kia contributing 79,424 units — a 19.32% year-on-year gain.

The broader Indian auto market has sustained strong momentum through July. Maruti Suzuki posted its highest-ever domestic and total monthly sales at 2.41 lakh units. Tata Motors dispatched 62,611 units domestically, up 58% year-on-year, while Mahindra's SUV volumes crossed 60,000 for the second consecutive month. Hyundai posted its highest-ever total sales above 75,000 units, with domestic volumes up 23%.

Kia's global parent has set an India sales target of 302,000 vehicles for calendar year 2026. With nearly 1.92 lakh units sold through seven months, the company has covered roughly 64% of that target with five months remaining.

What's Next

Kia plans to launch the Sorento Hybrid in India ahead of the festive season, adding a three-row hybrid SUV to a lineup that has so far leaned on conventional ICE and battery-electric powertrains. The company is also preparing new powertrain options across its existing range.

With more than 900 customer touchpoints across over 400 cities and an expanding certified pre-owned network, Kia's retail footprint continues to widen. The combination of a diversifying product portfolio and the approaching festive demand peak positions the company to sustain its double-digit growth trajectory through the second half of the year.
